_comment: Worst-case latency budgets in clock cycles, request edge to handler-start report on the trace port. Formula and every constant are explained in the README. Constants: S = 2 (irq_pnd and irq_buf registers), E = 9 (handler fetch hits the i-cache), R = 20 (one 64-byte line refill from IMEM), Rs = 52 (one line refill from the slow XBUS memory, MEM_LATE = 16), T = longest commit-to-commit time of one instruction in that loop (sim/logs/instr_cycles_smoke.txt).
_b2b_note: A later static cycle model of the B2B loop gives an upper bound of 118 cycles, above this budget of 111; the slowest B2B sample is 64 in sim/run_final and sim/run_restored and 67 in sim/run_final_serialmulshift and sim/run_fail_crit100 (2,008 to 2,009 samples per run). The budget is compiled into sw/irq_lat, and gate.py checks it against the bound each log reports, so raising it to 118 needs those runs repeated.

_derivation.BASE: S + 2T + E + 2R = 2 + 2*6 + 9 + 40 (T = 6: ALU op after a taken branch)
_derivation.LDST: S + 2T + E + 2R = 2 + 2*44 + 9 + 40 (T = 44: store to the slow memory)
_derivation.B2B: S + H + T + E + 2R = 2 + 54 + 6 + 9 + 40 (H = handler from the ACK store to mret = 54)
_derivation.ICOLD: S + 2T + E + Rs + T = 2 + 2*39 + 9 + 52 + 39 (T = 39: ALU op that waits for an IMEM refill after fence.i; one such refill can be in flight when the trap arrives)
